ON
December 10, 1945, Brother George
Caleb Kmgsley, Psi '05, was elected
to the Executive Councfl, to fill the unex
pired term of Brother Roswell Gray Ham,
Epsilon '14.
Brother Kmgsley was born in 1883 in
Livingston County, New York. He grad
uated from Danville High School in 1901
and Hamflton College with the degree of
A.B. in 1905. He received an
honorary
M.A. degree from Hamilton in 1910.
He was in business in New York, Phfla
delphia, Boston, Pittsburgh, Toronto and
Montreal, with the Library Bureau, from
1905 until, in 1915, he was made Western
Sales Manager of that Company with head
quarters in Chicago. When in 1926, the *
Library Bureau was
merged with Reming
ton Rand, Brother Kingsley took charge of
the Chicago business of the latter Com
pany until 1929, when he became con
nected with the Recording and Statistical

company organized to take
over the insurance service work of Rem
ington Rand. For the last ten years he has
been president of this company, which has
plants in Toronto, Danville, 111., and Boston,
and operating offices in a number of cities.
Its New York offices are at 102 Maiden
Lane.
Brother Kingsley is descended from
colonial stock, one of his ancestors having
settled ui New Bedford, Mass., in 1635.
He is a trustee of the Museum of the Amer
ican Indian, and of the Rockledge Founda
tion, a member of the University Club of
New York and the University Club in Chi
cago, the National Club in Toronto, the
Drug and Chemical Club in New York and
the Bankers Club in New York.
Brother Kingsley was married in 1910 to
Mary E. Crossett of Geneseo, N.Y., who is
deceased. Two of his sons were members of
Psi Upsflon, George Crossett Kingsley, Psi
'33, now a resident of New York, and James
Edward Crossett Kingsley, Phi '38. The lat

Gulf in the Philippines in 1945. Both sons
served in the armed forces, the former a
George Caleb Kingsley, Psi '05
First Lieutenant in the Army Air Corps
and the latter a Lieutenant (j.g.) in the
Navy.
Brother Kingsley lives at 18 East 8th
Street, New York City, and Geneseo, N.Y.

Obviously the way to begin was to get
a
thorough grounding in high finance and
American business, so Terry accepted a.
position with the investment counsel firm
of Scudder, Stevens and Clark in New
York City.
For the next six years Terry remamed in
WaU Street but kept his eyes and ears
open

The opportunity came in 1935 when the

C. T. S. Keep, Delta Delta '28
evolved in his mind and that of a few of

Terry sold it and in so

completely
